title: The AI race is moving beyond foundation models.
subtitle: The editorial conversation is widening toward agents, distribution, infrastructure, economics and human impact.

states.label: 1 YEAR AGO

states.synthesis: Attention is shifting from raw benchmarks toward distribution, agents and infrastructure economics. Human impact begins to appear as a faint but recurring theme.

perspectives.name: Technology
perspectives.summary: The technology perspective has retreated from leaderboard dominance to a quieter premise: capability still matters, but benchmarks no longer decide outcomes. Coverage now treats model performance as table stakes, framing frontier gains as background conditions rather than headline events. The open question is which capabilities—reasoning, reliability, autonomy—translate into durable advantage once parity becomes the norm.
perspectives.coreArgument: Raw capability is now table stakes; the story is what models enable.

perspectives.name: Platform
perspectives.summary: The platform perspective has matured from supporting argument into the race's central thesis. Coverage concentrates on distribution, defaults and ecosystems: agent interfaces, API moats and app-store analogies dominate the current conversation. The argument is that whoever owns the default entry point to AI—where users and developers actually land—captures the value that raw capability alone cannot secure.

perspectives.name: Infrastructure
perspectives.summary: The infrastructure perspective has moved from background context to binding constraint. Coverage focuses on physical limits: grid capacity, semiconductor supply and data-center buildouts now determine what deployment is feasible and at what pace. The argument is that compute access, not model access, separates serious competitors from aspirants—and that these constraints favor incumbents with capital and land.

perspectives.name: Economics
perspectives.summary: The economics perspective has accelerated around a single unresolved question: as inference costs collapse, where does durable value accrue? Coverage weighs a productivity paradox, competing theories of surplus capture, and cost-driven model selection. The through-line is that cheap intelligence may compress margins everywhere except at the choke points—distribution, compute and trust—where scarcity persists.

perspectives.name: Human Impact
perspectives.summary: The human-impact perspective has emerged from near-invisibility into a recurring editorial lens. Coverage now spans the future of work, education and creative attribution, asking who benefits from scaled deployment and who is displaced. Though still the newest perspective by volume, it increasingly supplies the evaluative standard against which the rest of the race is judged.
